**Title:** Which Dollar Broke? Separating Token Failures from Platform-Ledger Failures in Web Dollar Markets

**Abstract (297 words):**

Web price feeds and on-chain oracles average quotes from exchanges as if every USD price were in the same dollar. Some quote stablecoin tokens; others quote balances in an exchange's internal ledger, which reach the banking system only through the platform's rails. When those rails fail, the platform's dollar drifts from bank money, and the feed reports a platform failure as a price move. Work on feed reliability covers manipulation, staleness and outliers, and work on cross-exchange gaps links them to segmentation or exchange default risk. We know of no measure that separates token failures from ledger failures. This is hard: a ledger's value is never quoted directly, public prices are asynchronous trades that thin out under stress, and any one asset may carry its own shock. Our decomposition prices the platform's dollar through unpegged assets against venues whose rails stay open, splitting a dollar-quoted dislocation into token and ledger components, accepted only when unrelated assets agree and internal cross-rates hold. Across rail-cut episodes on three platforms from 2017 to 2023, the platform's dollar, not a token, moved on two: Bitfinex and Binance.US. On Bitfinex it fell by up to 844 bps, with BTC and ETH agreeing to within 7.2 bps. On both platforms it traded at a discount while exit was impaired and later at a premium. A volume-weighted BTC/USD index over these venues was off by at least 100 bps for 2,826 hours; dropping the venue-hours our rule flags removes 88% of them. On Bitfinex in 2018 the discount appeared 3 days before the deposit freeze was reported and about 6.5 months before regulators disclosed the loss behind it. In the March 2023 USDC run the method attributes all but 6% of the dislocation to the token. All findings are descriptive and use public data.

**Suggested keywords:** stablecoins; platform money; exchange ledgers; price feeds and oracles; Web measurement; natural experiment; reproducibility
